newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks recover, resource trade active.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks recover, resource trade active.

text.p: SPI Sycom 2690.0 +6.0 US 30yr cl 6.69 -0.03

*Stocks head back towards record territory after soft opening, miners active. Volume 204.6 million, value A$431.7 million, 998 traded, 330 steady, 292 up, 376 down
"It also looks like there is a bit of overseas support for the same levels. The bond market has rallied and that has probably helped, too," Bond said.
Leading miners BHP and Normandy were among the most active stocks in the morning session.

BHP shares were up 18 cents to A$19.45 at 12.50 p.m. (0250 GMT). Australia's biggest listed company announced earlier on Thursday it planned a A$500 million coal expansion with partners Central Queensland Coal Associates.
Over 12 million Normandy shares changed hands in morning trade with its price dropping two cents to A$1.60.
Dealers said nine million of the shares had been put through by Bain in two parcels shortly before 11.45 a.m. (0145 GMT).
Others said the market was still adjusting to an overnight drop of US$2.45 in the price of gold to US$338.90/40, close to its four-year low seen in February.
Nickel producer QNI also saw plenty of activity in its first session since Wednesday's announcement of a merger with South African mining house Gencor.
QNI shares were up six cents to A$2.74 on trade of 6.9 million and dealers and brokers were split on how they thought the market had accepted the merger.
"I'm surprised that they're not trading at a higher level. We think the announcement makes for a stronger company," said Ivan Mitchell, a broker from Brisbane brokerage Nevitts Ltd.
Other brokers and analysts said institutional investors had decided overnight the deal appeared more favourable to Gencor than QNI.
Macquarie Bank shares jumped by over three percent and were up 35 cents at A$11.36 at 1.15 p.m. (0115 GMT) as the banking sector picked up 37.9 points to move past 4,800.
Dealers attributed Macquarie's movement to its strong profit report earlier in June and successful infrastructure investment.
National Australia Bank rose 12 cents to A$18.77, Commonwealth Bank was up 10 cents to A$15.15 and ANZ rose 10 cents to A$9.65.
Westpac lifted six cents to A$7.81.
In other market news, yields on Australian bonds slipped slowly during the morning as the market looked for direction in the absence of any major data.
Yields on benchmark 10-year bonds remained just above the seven percent mark at 7.04 percent with the 10 year T-bond trading up 0.060 points 92.945.
A listless Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7490/95.
